# Women leaders widen girls’ ambitions through book

[Business](https://punchng.com/topics/business/)  October 14, 2026 12:12 am

Illustrative group photograph of African women leaders at the unveiling of A Letter to My Younger Self in Dakar, Senegal, on 10 October 2026.

By  [Justice Okamgba](https://punchng.com/author/justice-okamgbapunchng-com)

Kindly share this story:

Seventeen African women leaders from 12 countries have shared personal experiences and career lessons in a new bilingual book aimed at broadening the ambitions of younger generations of women across the continent.

The book, A Letter to My Younger Self, initiated by Aïda Diouf, telecommunications executive and 2026 Young Global Leader of the World Economic Forum, was officially released in bookshops in Dakar, Senegal, on 10 October 2026.

 The book features letters reflecting on the contributors’ doubts, challenges, turning points and lessons, spanning technology, finance, fashion, sports, media, the arts and civil society.

 In the foreword, internationally acclaimed Beninese singer Angélique Kidjo highlighted the courage required to revisit personal experiences honestly.

 “I want to honour the courage of every contributor to this book. The courage to tell your story truthfully, to look back at yourself from the most fragile and truthful place of all: the woman you once were, the one who doubted,” Kidjo wrote.

 Diouf said the project’s ambition extended beyond publication to reaching young women who could benefit from the contributors’ experiences.

 “This book is a milestone, not an end in itself. Our ambition is for these words to travel, to reach young girls who need them, and to open up new possibilities, spark conversations or change the course of a life,” she stated.

 The contributors include Founder and Creative Director of Ghanaian fashion label Christie Brown, Aisha Ayensu; Senior Vice-President and Group Country Manager for West and Central Africa at Visa, Aminata Kane; Head of Africa at GSMA, Angela Wamola; Chief Executive of Benin’s Sèmè City innovation hub, Claude Borna; Regional Director at Wave Mobile Money, Coura Sène; and Cameroonian novelist Djaïli Amal.

 Others are Beninese Chef Georgiana Viou, whose restaurant Rouge received a Michelin star in 2023; Founder of Senegal’s École des Sables, Germaine Acogny; Nigerian democracy and women’s rights activist Hafsat Abiola; Managing Director of Spotify for Sub-Saharan Africa, Jocelyne Muhutu-Remy; Congolese women’s rights activist Julienne Lusenge; and President of Africa International Group, Marie-Roger Biloa.

 The list also includes Vice-President and Chief Executive of Les Eaux Minérales d’Oulmès, Miriem Chaqroun; Tunisian tennis player and former world number two, Ons Jabeur; Angolan Architect and Curator Paula Nascimento; Founder of Ivory Coast’s SEPHIS Foundation, Sefora Kodjo; and Kenyan Photographer Thandiwe Muriu.

 Their letters challenge conventional ideas about leadership, identity and success. Ayensu urges young women to embrace African heritage, writing, “Belong first to yourself. Then to your continent. Then to the world.”

 Wamola encourages women facing barriers in technology, telling her younger self, “You are not a support act. You are a leader-in-waiting.”

 Meanwhile, Kane reflects on professional self-doubt, while Borna argues that women should see others’ achievements as evidence of what is possible rather than as competition.

 The initiative plans to distribute 10,000 copies free of charge across more than 10 African countries, beginning with Senegal, Morocco and Ivory Coast. Revenue from bookshop sales will be reinvested in the non-profit project to support distribution and community activities.

 The first distribution began at John F. Kennedy High School, an all-girls school in Dakar, where 50 students were expected to receive copies during a gathering promoting reading and intergenerational dialogue. The school’s majorettes have participated in Senegal’s Independence Day parade since 1975, a tradition associated with choreographer Acogny and master drummer Doudou Rose.

 The initiative is led by ALTMYS, with partners including publisher La Croisée des Chemins, HEC Paris Executive Education, Shine to Lead and Les Cultur’Elles. Nigerian illustrator Renike, also known as Morenike Olosanya, contributed to the book’s visual presentation, while logistics company PAPS is supporting storage and distribution.

 The organisers intend to expand the initiative through universities, libraries, associations and non-governmental organisations, using the women’s stories to encourage mentorship, knowledge-sharing and wider aspirations among younger African women.
